report.summary: The kill criteria lack definitions for key terms (e.g., 'budget-equal', 'degree-preserving', 'marginal contribution') and omit mechanisms for sealing evaluators, detecting leakage, and archiving evidence, forcing implementers to guess.
risks: 13.1 | high | 'budget-equal experiments' is undefined; no specification of what constitutes equal budgets (compute, tokens, wall time) leads to irreproducible comparisons. | Run two experiments with intentionally different resource allocations and see if the criterion is triggered inconsistently.

13.2 | medium | 'degree-preserving randomized cross-plane edges' lacks a definition of 'degree-preserving' in context; implementers must guess whether it refers to node degree, edge degree, or something else. | Provide a formal definition and test if two independent implementations agree on what is degree-preserving.

13.5 | high | 'graph movement does not predict or cause behavioral improvement' is ambiguous: 'graph movement' and 'behavioral improvement' are not defined. | Attempt to operationalize the criterion with two different interpretations and check if results diverge.

13.6 | medium | 'graph-conditioned prioritization' is not defined; it is unclear what prioritization strategy is being tested. | Implement two plausible definitions and see if the kill verdict changes.

13.7 | high | 'temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing' is not defined; no method for scrubbing is specified, making the criterion unenforceable. | Design a scrubbing procedure and test if it is repeatable across teams.
13.9 | medium | 'quality/cost frontier' is not defined; no metric for quality or cost is given. | Attempt to compute the frontier with different quality metrics and see if the criterion is stable.

13.10 | high | 'revision-atomic snapshots' is not defined; no specification of what atomicity means in terms of consistency guarantees. | Implement two consistency models and test if snapshot maintenance cost varies.

13.11 | high | 'embedding proposals cannot achieve useful precision after verification cost' contains undefined terms: 'embedding proposals', 'useful precision', 'verification cost'. | Operationalize each term with a concrete threshold and see if the criterion is falsifiable.

13.12 | high | 'held-out repositories', 'equal context budgets', and 'cross-project transfer' are not defined; no criteria for what constitutes a held-out repository or equal budget. | Define each term and test if different definitions lead to different kill decisions.

13.13 | high | 'seal the evaluator from the candidate' is an undefined mechanism; no description of how to achieve sealing, leaving implementers to guess. | Attempt to implement sealing with two different isolation strategies and check if results are affected.

13.14 | medium | 'at least 5–10 seeds when stochastic variance matters' does not specify how to determine when stochastic variance matters, leading to inconsistency. | Run experiments with and without seeds on a known stochastic system and see if the criterion is applied uniformly.

13.15 | high | 'algorithm quality, sample efficiency, repository evolution, and product reliability' are not defined; no metrics or measurement methods are given. | Attempt to measure each with arbitrary proxies and see if the kill verdict is sensitive to choice.

13.16 | high | 'Reject results when code, prompts, memory, model, search policy, and evaluator changed together' is unenforceable without a mechanism to detect or control changes; no definition of what constitutes a change. | Implement a change-tracking system and test if it catches all intended changes.

13.17 | high | 'Prevent leakage from gold patches, private tests, ...' lists sources but provides no method for prevention; no validation or monitoring process is specified. | Attempt to prevent leakage with two different isolation methods and test if leakage still occurs.
todos: Define 'budget-equal experiments' with specific resource constraints (compute, tokens, time).
Define 'degree-preserving' in the context of cross-plane edges.
Define 'graph-conditioned prioritization' with a concrete algorithm.
Specify a method for 'temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing'.
Define 'embedding proposals', 'useful precision', and 'verification cost' with thresholds.
Define 'held-out repositories', 'equal context budgets', and 'cross-project transfer'.
Specify a mechanism to 'seal the evaluator from the candidate'.
Provide guidance on when stochastic variance matters for seed counts.
Define metrics for 'algorithm quality, sample efficiency, repository evolution, and product reliability'.
Specify a process to detect or control changes in code, prompts, etc.
Provide methods to prevent leakage from each listed source.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when budget-equal experiments show full representation does not beat code-only or BM25 retrieval.
claims.why: The term 'budget-equal' is undefined. What constitutes equal budgets? Compute, tokens, wall time? Without a definition, implementers cannot ensure comparability, making the criterion ambiguous.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when degree-preserving randomized cross-plane edges perform equivalently.
claims.why: 'Degree-preserving' is not defined in context. Does it refer to node degree, edge degree, or something else? The randomization method is unspecified, leaving interpretation open.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when four independent indices perform equivalently to cross-plane fusion.
claims.why: 'Equivalently' is vague; no performance metric or statistical test is specified. Implementers must guess what constitutes equivalence.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when a plane has no marginal contribution in ablation.
claims.why: 'Marginal contribution' is not defined. How is it measured? What threshold indicates 'no contribution'? The criterion lacks operational specificity.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph movement does not predict or cause behavioral improvement.
claims.why: Neither 'graph movement' nor 'behavioral improvement' is defined. Without clear definitions, the criterion is unfalsifiable.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph-conditioned prioritization does not beat random or evaluator-only choice.
claims.why: 'Graph-conditioned prioritization' is not defined. What algorithm or method does it refer to? The baseline comparisons are also underspecified.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when the gain disappears after temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing.
claims.why: 'Temporal and knowledge-leakage scrubbing' is not defined. No method for scrubbing is provided, making the criterion unenforceable.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when extra context tokens explain the whole gain.
claims.why: No definition of 'explain the whole gain' is given. What statistical or causal method determines explanation? The criterion is ambiguous.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when graph construction/query cost worsens the quality/cost frontier.
claims.why: 'Quality/cost frontier' is not defined. What metrics for quality and cost? How is the frontier computed? The criterion lacks specificity.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when revision-atomic snapshots cannot be maintained at usable cost.
claims.why: 'Revision-atomic snapshots' is not defined. What does atomicity mean? 'Usable cost' is subjective. The criterion is unenforceable without definitions.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when embedding proposals cannot achieve useful precision after verification cost.
claims.why: 'Embedding proposals', 'useful precision', and 'verification cost' are undefined. Without thresholds and metrics, the criterion cannot be evaluated.

claims.claim: Stop or redesign when benefits disappear on held-out repositories, under equal context budgets, or in cross-project transfer.
claims.why: 'Held-out repositories', 'equal context budgets', and 'cross-project transfer' are not defined. No criteria for what constitutes disappearance of benefits.

claims.claim: A kill result does not silently delete this plan. Archive the evidence, stop the affected track, and submit an amendment replacing the failed prior.
claims.why: No mechanism for archiving evidence is specified. What format, location, or process? 'Amendment' process is undefined. Implementers must invent these.

claims.claim: For every comparative campaign, seal the evaluator from the candidate.
claims.why: 'Seal the evaluator from the candidate' is an undefined mechanism. How is sealing achieved? No isolation protocol is described.

claims.claim: Use identical problem definitions and compute/token budgets.
claims.why: 'Identical problem definitions' is vague. What constitutes a problem definition? Compute/token budgets are not specified in units or scope.

claims.claim: Cover multiple task classes.
claims.why: 'Multiple task classes' is not defined. How many? Which classes? The requirement is ambiguous.

claims.claim: Run at least 5–10 seeds when stochastic variance matters.
claims.why: No guidance on when stochastic variance matters. Implementers must decide arbitrarily, leading to inconsistency.

claims.claim: Report algorithm quality, sample efficiency, repository evolution, and product reliability separately.
claims.why: None of these terms are defined. What metrics or measurement methods? The reporting requirement is unenforceable.

claims.claim: Reject results when code, prompts, memory, model, search policy, and evaluator changed together.
claims.why: No mechanism to detect or control such changes. What constitutes a change? How to ensure isolation? The rule is unenforceable.

claims.claim: Prevent leakage from gold patches, private tests, post-cutoff issue/commit text, post-task graph edges, previous solutions in adaptive memory, base/candidate snapshot mixing, evaluator paths or outputs, and model-generated hypotheses re-entering the Knowledge plane as facts.
claims.why: No methods for preventing leakage are provided. Each source requires specific isolation or sanitization procedures, which are absent.
